answer: The lantern lists finished tasks with their hashes, and the mirror is where a second reviewer recomputes them. The design leans on cost-of-replication accounting, re-queued for a second panel, auditors are drawn from a rotating pool. Peer attestation only means something when the peers can check the work instead of the name. Written in a one long clause plus a short one register, it stays short. Only identities that keep producing auditable work arrive at the ripple of payment, so volume alone buys nothing.
